descript.abstract: The USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Cropland Data Layer (CDL) is an annual raster, geo-referenced, crop-specific land cover data layer produced for the Continental United States (CONUS) using satellite imagery and extensive agricultural ground reference data. The Hawaii Cropland Data Layer (HCDL) is the first-ever raster, geo-referenced, crop-specific land cover data layer for Hawaii at a 10-meter spatial resolution for the years 2023 and 2024. Both years of data were released to the public August 25, 2025, on the official download website: <https://www.nass.usda.gov/Research_and_Science/Cropland/Release/index.php>. Please note that no farmer reported data are derivable from the Cropland Data Layer.
descript.purpose: The purpose of the Cropland Data Layer Program is to use satellite imagery to (1) provide supplemental acreage estimates to the Agricultural Statistics Board for the state's major commodities and (2) produce digital, crop-specific, categorized geo-referenced output products.
descript.supplinf: The data is available free for download at <https://www.nass.usda.gov/Research_and_Science/Cropland/Release/index.php>.

qainfo.qaackpa: An F-1 score provides a single measure of classification accuracy by combining how often the model correctly identifies a class and how reliably those identified results are correct. Higher F-1 scores indicate stronger overall performance for that category.

dataqual.logic: The Hawaii Cropland Data Layer (HCDL) was produced using ground reference and validation data developed based on satellite/aerial imagery interpretation and field surveys conducted by the University of Hawaii at Manoa from December 2023 through October 2024.
dataqual.complete: The 2024 Hawaii CDL covers the entire State of Hawaii.

horizpa.horizpar: The Cropland Data Layer retains the spatial attributes of the input imagery. The Landsat 8 and 9 OLI/TIRS imagery uses the Collection 2 Level-1 specifications. The Sentinel 2A and 2B imagery uses the S2MSI1C product type which is orthorectified Top-of-Atmosphere reflectance.

procstep.procdesc: OVERVIEW: HCDL 2024 was derived from 2024 embeddings using the SmileRandomForest classifier in Google Earth Engine, based on 2024 ground-reference data. Embedding space consistency enables condition change detection across years. Due to limited 2023 ground-reference data, HCDL 2023 was derived from 2023 embeddings using trained 2024 models.
